## Getting started

1. Install Python 3.10+ and at least one of Claude Code, Codex or Antigravity, and log in to it.
2. First run, from the checkout (the `trirouter` command does not exist yet):

   ```bash
   python install.py --dry-run     # preview every change
   python install.py               # interactive setup (same as `python install.py setup`)
   ```

3. Setup writes the `trirouter` launcher to `~/.trirouter/bin` and puts that folder on your PATH
   (Windows: the user PATH, never the system one; macOS / Linux: a link in `~/.local/bin`, and setup prints the
   line to add to your shell profile if that folder is not on PATH). **Reopen your terminal**, then:

   ```bash
   trirouter help                  # the command list
   trirouter doctor                # health report
   ```

   Setup also installs tab completion for your shell (PowerShell, bash, zsh or fish): type `trirouter `, a
   few letters, and press Tab to complete commands, subcommands, flags and flag values.

If you move the checkout, run `python install.py` from its new place once: the launcher and the hooks are
re-pointed. `python install.py <command>` and `python -m trirouter <command>` always keep working and
behave like `trirouter <command>`.

## Conventions

* `trirouter <command> [subcommand] [flags]`; flags may come in any order after the command. `--flag=value`
  and `--flag value` are equivalent.
* Every command declares the flags it accepts. An unknown or not-applicable flag, a value flag without a value
  or a boolean flag given a value is an error: exit status 2, a "did you mean" suggestion and a pointer to the
  help page.
* `-h`, `--help` anywhere after a command shows its page; `trirouter help <command>` does the same.
* Short flags: `-h` help, `-y` --yes, `-n` --dry-run, `-a` --apply (boolean ones can be combined: `-yn`).
* Flags marked "remembered" are saved in `~/.trirouter/config.json` when the command writes, and apply to
  later runs.
* `trirouter --version` (`-V`) prints the version; `trirouter -h` shows the command list.
* Ctrl+C stops a command at once (Ctrl+D does the same, also at a question): one line "Interrupted: nothing was
  left half-written." on stderr, exit status 130, started child processes ended, files written atomically.
* Exit status: 0 success, 2 usage error, 1 the command ran but failed, 130 interrupted.

## Common tasks

| I want to | Command |
| --- | --- |
| See what setup would do | `trirouter setup --dry-run` |
| Check that everything works | `trirouter doctor` |
| Re-scan skills after adding some to `~/.skills` | `trirouter skills --apply` |
| See what is in quarantine and when it is deleted | `trirouter quarantine` |
| Get a quarantined skill back | `trirouter quarantine restore <name>`<br>`trirouter skills --apply` |
| Keep quarantined skills a week instead of 3 days | `trirouter skills --apply --quarantine-days=7` |
| Never delete quarantined skills automatically | `trirouter skills --apply --quarantine-days=0` |
| Get the routing decision for a sub-task from a script | `trirouter route --json "add a CSV export"` |
| Check for new or retired models now | `trirouter models --discover` |
| Turn the daily model check off | `trirouter models --auto=off` |
| Print the version | `trirouter --version` |
| Reach this computer from a phone | `trirouter remote --name "My PC"` |
| Update tab completion, agents and docs after a pull or a change | `trirouter sync` |
| Remove everything the installer added | `trirouter uninstall` |

## setup

Detect the AI tools, connect hooks and MCP, link and scan skills.

```
trirouter setup [-y] [-n] [--providers=LIST] [--jev-token=TOKEN] [--remote[=NAME]] [options]
```

Interactive setup in five steps: (1) detect Claude Code, Codex and Antigravity and help you log in; (2) the JEV / TypeSafe token or an OpenRouter key (optional; without one the built-in local model decides); (3) hooks and the MCP server for every logged-in tool, the `trirouter` command itself and its tab completion in your shell profile (PowerShell, bash, zsh or fish; skip it with --no-completion); (4) the shared skill folder ~/.skills: existing skills are moved there, scanned with SkillSpector when it is installed, linked into every tool, and expired quarantine entries are purged; worker agents are generated; (5) optional remote access and speech-to-text.

Every change is shown first, a changed config file keeps a .bak copy, and re-running is safe. `python install.py` with no arguments does the same. A saved JEV key is stored protected, and a plaintext key left by an older version is protected on the next save (see `trirouter keys`).

An install from before the rename (state folder ~/.jev-router) is migrated first: the folder moves to ~/.trirouter, and the hooks, MCP entries (renamed to `trirouter`), PATH entry and remote-access services that point into it are rewritten. A dry run only reports this. `skills --apply`, `remote`, `models` and `uninstall` do the same before they write.

| Flag | Value | Default | Remembered | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-y`, `--yes` | - | off | no | Never prompt: answer every question with its default. Unattended runs move, quarantine or delete nothing that needs a decision. |
| `-n`, `--dry-run` | - | off | no | Show what would change and change nothing, config.json included. |
| `--providers` | `LIST` | every installed, logged-in tool | no | Comma-separated tools to connect: claude, codex, antigravity. |
| `--jev-token` | `TOKEN` | none | yes (typesafe_api_key or openrouter_api_key) | A TypeSafe token, or an OpenRouter key (sk-or-...). Saved protected: encrypted with Windows DPAPI for your account, owner-only file mode 0600 on macOS and Linux. The environment variables TYPESAFE_API_KEY and JEV_OPENROUTER_API_KEY work too and win over the saved key. |
| `--openrouter-key` | `KEY` | none | yes (openrouter_api_key) | An OpenRouter key; same as --jev-token=sk-or-... |
| `--remote` | `NAME` (optional) | ask | yes (remote_name) | Also set up remote access, under NAME (default: the saved name or the hostname). |
| `--workdir` | `DIR` | the checkout | yes (remote_workdir) | Folder remote Claude sessions start in. Only used together with remote access. |
| `--no-migrate` | - | off | no | Do not move the skills of other tools into ~/.skills. |
| `--no-completion` | - | off | no | Do not install tab completion for `trirouter` into your shell profile (`uninstall` removes it again). |
| `--allow-skill` | `NAME,...` | none | yes (skillscan.allow) | Never ask about these skills and restore them from quarantine. Names are added to the saved list. |
| `--scan-llm` | `on|off` | off | yes (skillscan.llm) | Add SkillSpector's LLM analysis to the static scan. Skill content then leaves the machine through SkillSpector's own provider settings. |
| `--accept-flagged` | - | off | no (this run only) | Keep every skill now rated DO_NOT_INSTALL without asking, like answering "none" to the quarantine question. Bound to the skill's current content: it is asked about again when it changes. |
| `--quarantine-days` | `N` | 3 | yes (skillscan.quarantine_days) | Days a quarantined skill is kept before it is deleted for good. 0 = never delete. |
| `--catalog-only` | `PATTERN,...` | none | yes (skills.catalog_only) | Hub skills whose folder name matches one of these patterns (fnmatch, e.g. gke-*,google-*) stay in ~/.skills and in the catalog but are not linked into Claude Code or Codex, so their descriptions do not load into every session; the router still names them with their path and the MCP get_skill tool serves them. Replaces the saved list; `none` clears it. Antigravity reads the whole hub and keeps seeing them. |
| `-h`, `--help` | - | - | - | Show this help page and exit. |

**Changes:** Changes files; preview with --dry-run.

Examples:

```bash
trirouter setup    # interactive setup (python install.py alone does the same)
trirouter setup --dry-run    # show every change, write nothing
trirouter setup --yes --providers=claude,codex    # unattended, only these two tools
trirouter setup --jev-token=sk-or-...    # add an OpenRouter key and keep the rest
trirouter setup --yes --remote="My PC"    # also set up remote access
```

**Exit status:** 0 on success. 2 on a usage error. 1 when no logged-in tool was found.

**See also:** [keys](#keys), [models](#models), [skills](#skills), [remote](#remote), [doctor](#doctor), [uninstall](#uninstall)

## keys

Protect the API keys saved in config.json.

```
trirouter keys [-a] [-n]
```

Older versions kept the TypeSafe token or OpenRouter key as plain text in ~/.trirouter/config.json. This command re-writes it protected: on Windows encrypted with the Data Protection API (DPAPI), so the value opens only for your user account on this machine (a copy of config.json on another machine or account holds an unusable blob and the router falls back to the built-in local model); on macOS and Linux the standard library has no keystore, so the key stays a string and the file is limited to its owner (mode 0600). Plain-text values stay readable until they are migrated; the environment variables always win.

No plaintext copy is left behind: the previous config.json is kept as config.json.bak WITHOUT its key, and the key is also removed from older backups next to it (config.json.*). Without --apply the command only previews; `trirouter doctor` reports the state. A key saved with `setup --jev-token` is stored protected right away, `setup` also removes plaintext keys from old backups.

| Flag | Value | Default | Remembered | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-a`, `--apply` | - | off | no | Write the changes. Without it the command only previews them. |
| `-n`, `--dry-run` | - | off | no | Show what would change and change nothing, config.json included. |
| `-h`, `--help` | - | - | - | Show this help page and exit. |

**Changes:** Preview by default; --apply writes.

Examples:

```bash
trirouter keys    # show what would be protected
trirouter keys --apply    # protect the key and scrub the backups
```

**Exit status:** 0 on success. 2 on a usage error. 1 when a key could not be protected.

**See also:** [setup](#setup), [doctor](#doctor)

## models

Find new models, drop retired ones, test which ones your accounts can use.

```
trirouter models [-n]
trirouter models --discover [-n]
trirouter models --auto=on|off
trirouter models --main=FAMILY|off [--subagent-model=FAMILY|off] [-n]
```

Compares what each tool offers today with the models the router knows. Codex: `codex debug models`; Antigravity: `agy models`; Claude Code: the model aliases `claude --help` names (only generic family aliases such as haiku, sonnet, opus or fable -- never a dated model ID or a mode alias). A model seen for the first time is tried with a one-word prompt (Codex, Claude; about 10-60 s each) and becomes selectable when it answers; a model that is no longer offered is taken out of the selection (Claude: only after a prompt confirms it is gone). A check that cannot run -- tool missing, not logged in, network error -- changes nothing. Results are stored per user in ~/.trirouter/models.local.json, never in the repository, and the worker agents are regenerated when something changed. Effort levels outside the policy (ultra) are always dropped.

Without --discover the command also sends the one-word prompt to every known Codex model, the full account check. --discover runs only the cheap daily check, which also runs by itself in the background at most once every 24 hours, started by a Claude Code session start or a Codex / Antigravity prompt; the outcome is logged to ~/.trirouter/logs/model_discovery.log, the next Claude Code session is told once what changed, and `trirouter doctor` shows the last check. --auto=off switches the background check off.

--main and --subagent-model set Claude Code's own defaults: the model new sessions start on (~/.claude/settings.json `model`) and the model of subagents that name none, such as general-purpose (env CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL; trirouter's worker agents keep their own models). Most prompts are answered in the session itself, so a cheaper main model (sonnet) with the router escalating hard work to opus / fable workers costs far less than an opus session. Both are remembered and re-applied by setup; `off` removes the setting.

| Flag | Value | Default | Remembered | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--discover` | - | off | no | Only the daily check: list every tool's models, try only the new ones (and ones offered again). |
| `--auto` | `on|off` | on | yes (model_discovery.auto) | Switch the automatic daily check on or off. Given alone, only the setting is saved. |
| `--main` | `FAMILY|off` | unchanged | yes (claude.main_model) | Claude Code's default model for new sessions (haiku, sonnet, opus or fable); off removes it. |
| `--subagent-model` | `FAMILY|off` | unchanged | yes (claude.subagent_model) | The model of Claude subagents that name none (general-purpose, plugin agents); off removes it. |
| `-n`, `--dry-run` | - | off | no | Show what would change and change nothing, config.json included. |
| `-h`, `--help` | - | - | - | Show this help page and exit. |

**Changes:** Changes files (models.local.json, worker agents, ~/.claude/settings.json); preview with --dry-run.

Examples:

```bash
trirouter models --discover    # the daily check now
trirouter models --discover --dry-run    # show what it would add or remove, save nothing
trirouter models    # full check: also try every known Codex model
trirouter models --auto=off    # no automatic daily check
trirouter models --main=sonnet --subagent-model=sonnet    # cheap sessions; the router escalates
```

**Exit status:** 0 on success. 2 on a usage error. 1 when another model check is already running.

**See also:** [skills](#skills), [doctor](#doctor)

## skills

Scan and re-link skills, regenerate worker agents, rebuild the catalog.

```
trirouter skills [-a] [-y] [--allow-skill=NAME,...] [--scan-llm=on|off] [--accept-flagged] [--quarantine-days=N] [--catalog-only=PATTERN,...]
```

Scans every third-party skill in ~/.skills with NVIDIA SkillSpector (when installed), links the skills into Claude Code and Codex, registers the folder with Antigravity, regenerates the worker agents from config/models.json + config/targets.json and rebuilds the skill catalog. Expired quarantine entries are purged.

A skill rated DO_NOT_INSTALL is not decided one by one: after all scans you are asked once -- [a]ll / [n]one / [s]elect (default: none) -- which of them go to quarantine (~/.trirouter/quarantine, linked nowhere, deleted after 3 days). A skill you keep is remembered for its exact content. With --yes or without a terminal nothing is quarantined and only a warning is printed.

| Flag | Value | Default | Remembered | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-a`, `--apply` | - | off | no | Write the changes. Without it the command only previews them. |
| `-y`, `--yes` | - | off | no | Never prompt: answer every question with its default. Unattended runs move, quarantine or delete nothing that needs a decision. |
| `-n`, `--dry-run` | - | off | no | Show what would change and change nothing, config.json included. |
| `--allow-skill` | `NAME,...` | none | yes (skillscan.allow) | Never ask about these skills and restore them from quarantine. Names are added to the saved list. |
| `--scan-llm` | `on|off` | off | yes (skillscan.llm) | Add SkillSpector's LLM analysis to the static scan. Skill content then leaves the machine through SkillSpector's own provider settings. |
| `--accept-flagged` | - | off | no (this run only) | Keep every skill now rated DO_NOT_INSTALL without asking, like answering "none" to the quarantine question. Bound to the skill's current content: it is asked about again when it changes. |
| `--quarantine-days` | `N` | 3 | yes (skillscan.quarantine_days) | Days a quarantined skill is kept before it is deleted for good. 0 = never delete. |
| `--catalog-only` | `PATTERN,...` | none | yes (skills.catalog_only) | Hub skills whose folder name matches one of these patterns (fnmatch, e.g. gke-*,google-*) stay in ~/.skills and in the catalog but are not linked into Claude Code or Codex, so their descriptions do not load into every session; the router still names them with their path and the MCP get_skill tool serves them. Replaces the saved list; `none` clears it. Antigravity reads the whole hub and keeps seeing them. |
| `-h`, `--help` | - | - | - | Show this help page and exit. |

**Changes:** Preview by default; --apply writes.

Examples:

```bash
trirouter skills    # preview what would be linked, quarantined or purged
trirouter skills --apply    # scan, ask the quarantine question once, link
trirouter skills --apply --accept-flagged    # keep every flagged skill after a review
trirouter skills --apply --allow-skill=docx,xlsx    # trust two skills for good
trirouter skills --apply --scan-llm=on    # add the LLM analysis to the scan
trirouter skills --apply --catalog-only=gke-*,google-*    # keep rarely used skills out of every session
```

**Exit status:** 0 on success. 2 on a usage error (unknown or misused option, missing argument). 1 when the command ran but failed.

**See also:** [quarantine](#quarantine), [setup](#setup), [doctor](#doctor)

## quarantine

List, restore or purge skills the scan moved to quarantine.

```
trirouter quarantine [list]
trirouter quarantine restore NAME... [-n]
trirouter quarantine purge [--all] [-y] [-n] [--quarantine-days=N]
```

A skill moved to quarantine (~/.trirouter/quarantine) is linked nowhere and left out of the catalog. It is deleted for good after 3 days (setting skillscan.quarantine_days; 0 = never) -- automatically at every `setup`, every `skills --apply` and at most every 6 hours when Claude Code starts a session.

Subcommands: list (default), restore, purge. Run `trirouter help quarantine <subcommand>` for each.

| Flag | Value | Default | Remembered | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-h`, `--help` | - | - | - | Show this help page and exit. |

**Changes:** Changes nothing by itself; see the subcommands.

Examples:

```bash
trirouter quarantine    # list the quarantined skills
trirouter quarantine restore docx    # bring a skill back
trirouter quarantine purge    # delete the expired ones now
```

**Exit status:** 0 on success. 2 on a usage error (unknown or misused option, missing argument). 1 when the command ran but failed.

**See also:** [quarantine list](#quarantine-list), [quarantine restore](#quarantine-restore), [quarantine purge](#quarantine-purge), [skills](#skills)

### quarantine list

Show quarantined skills and when they will be deleted.

```
trirouter quarantine [list]
```

One line per quarantined skill: name, quarantine date, the date it is purged (and the time left) and the scan's risk score. The purge date uses the current retention setting.

| Flag | Value | Default | Remembered | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-h`, `--help` | - | - | - | Show this help page and exit. |

**Changes:** Changes nothing.

Examples:

```bash
trirouter quarantine    # same as `quarantine list`
```

**Exit status:** 0 on success. 2 on a usage error (unknown or misused option, missing argument). 1 when the command ran but failed.

**See also:** [quarantine restore](#quarantine-restore), [quarantine purge](#quarantine-purge)

### quarantine restore

Move a quarantined skill back into ~/.skills.

```
trirouter quarantine restore NAME... [-n]
```

Moves the newest quarantined copy of each NAME back to ~/.skills/NAME, provided that name is free, and adds it to skillscan.allow like --allow-skill does, so it is not flagged again. It is linked into the tools by the next `trirouter skills --apply`.

Arguments: NAME... one or more quarantined skill names (see `quarantine list`).

| Flag | Value | Default | Remembered | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-n`, `--dry-run` | - | off | no | Show what would change and change nothing, config.json included. |
| `-h`, `--help` | - | - | - | Show this help page and exit. |

**Changes:** Changes files; preview with --dry-run.

Examples:

```bash
trirouter quarantine restore docx    # restore one skill
trirouter quarantine restore docx xlsx -n    # preview restoring two
trirouter skills --apply    # then re-link
```

**Exit status:** 0 on success. 2 on a usage error. 1 when a name was not found or the hub already has that name.

**See also:** [quarantine list](#quarantine-list), [skills](#skills)

### quarantine purge

Delete expired quarantine entries now.

```
trirouter quarantine purge [--all] [-y] [-n] [--quarantine-days=N]
```

Permanently deletes the quarantined skills whose retention has run out (folder and metadata). With --all it deletes every entry, expired or not, after a confirmation. Only entries directly inside ~/.trirouter/quarantine are ever deleted; links are never followed.

| Flag | Value | Default | Remembered | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--all` | - | off | no | Delete every quarantined skill, not only the expired ones. Asks first. |
| `-y`, `--yes` | - | off | no | Never prompt: answer every question with its default. Unattended runs move, quarantine or delete nothing that needs a decision. |
| `-n`, `--dry-run` | - | off | no | Show what would change and change nothing, config.json included. |
| `--quarantine-days` | `N` | 3 | yes (skillscan.quarantine_days) | Days a quarantined skill is kept before it is deleted for good. 0 = never delete. |
| `-h`, `--help` | - | - | - | Show this help page and exit. |

**Changes:** Changes files (deletes for good); preview with --dry-run.

Examples:

```bash
trirouter quarantine purge    # delete the expired entries
trirouter quarantine purge --dry-run    # show which ones
trirouter quarantine purge --all    # delete everything, after a yes
trirouter quarantine purge --quarantine-days=7    # keep entries a week from now on
```

**Exit status:** 0 on success. 2 on a usage error. 1 when --all was not confirmed (nothing deleted).

**See also:** [quarantine list](#quarantine-list), [skills](#skills)

## remote

Set up or remove phone / other-device access.

```
trirouter remote [--name=NAME] [--workdir=DIR] [--start-session=on|off] [-n]
trirouter remote --remove [-n]
```

Starts each tool's own remote service at logon (Claude Code Remote Control, Antigravity and Codex), under one machine name. At logon only the connection opens: no Claude session is created until you start one from the Claude app or claude.ai/code (or make a terminal session reachable with /remote-control); the ChatGPT app and antigravity.google.com work the same way. See docs/remote-access.md.

| Flag | Value | Default | Remembered | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--name` | `NAME` | saved name or hostname | yes (remote_name) | The machine name shown on your other devices. |
| `--workdir` | `DIR` | saved folder or the checkout | yes (remote_workdir) | Folder remote Claude sessions start in; it must be a trusted Claude Code folder. |
| `--start-session` | `on|off` | off | yes (remote_start_session) | on: Claude's server also pre-creates one session in the folder at every logon (the old behaviour). off: only the connection; sessions start when you open one. |
| `--remove` | - | off | no | Remove the remote-access services instead of creating them. |
| `-n`, `--dry-run` | - | off | no | Show what would change and change nothing, config.json included. |
| `-h`, `--help` | - | - | - | Show this help page and exit. |

**Changes:** Changes files and system services; preview with --dry-run.

Examples:

```bash
trirouter remote --name "My PC"    # set up under a name
trirouter remote --name "My PC" --workdir ~/code    # choose the working folder
trirouter remote --start-session=on    # also pre-create a Claude session at logon
trirouter remote --remove    # undo
```

**Exit status:** 0 on success. 2 on a usage error (unknown or misused option, missing argument). 1 when the command ran but failed.

**See also:** [setup](#setup), [doctor](#doctor)

## sync

Bring everything generated from the sources up to date (after a pull or a change).

```
trirouter sync [--check | -n]
trirouter sync --pre-commit
```

One step after every development round or `git pull`, so new commands, flags and models work everywhere: rewrites the installed tab-completion scripts from the manual (shell profiles are left alone), regenerates the worker agents of the tools that already have generated ones (from templates/agents, targets.json and models.json) and, in a trirouter checkout, regenerates docs/cli.md and sets git's core.hooksPath to .githooks (never over another hooks folder or your own .git/hooks). The daily background check refreshes the completion scripts and agents by itself.

The checkout's git pre-commit hook runs `trirouter sync --pre-commit`: the sync, `git add docs/cli.md` when it was regenerated, a reminder when user-visible files are staged without CHANGELOG.md, the tests and, when routing code is staged (core, lang, distill, config, eval), the routing evaluation. A failure stops the commit; `git commit --no-verify` skips the hook once.

| Flag | Value | Default | Remembered | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--check` | - | off | no | Change nothing; exit 1 when something is out of date (for CI). |
| `--pre-commit` | - | off | no | What the git pre-commit hook runs: sync, stage docs/cli.md, tests, evaluation. Only in a trirouter checkout. |
| `-n`, `--dry-run` | - | off | no | Show what would change and change nothing, config.json included. |
| `-h`, `--help` | - | - | - | Show this help page and exit. |

**Changes:** Changes files; preview with --dry-run or --check.

Examples:

```bash
trirouter sync    # after a pull or a change
trirouter sync --check    # is anything out of date?
trirouter sync --pre-commit    # the checks the git hook runs, by hand
```

**Exit status:** 0 on success. 2 on a usage error. 1 when --check found something out of date, an item failed, or a --pre-commit check failed.

**See also:** [setup](#setup), [skills](#skills), [doctor](#doctor)

## daemon

The local hook daemon: Claude Code hooks without a Python start per prompt.

```
trirouter daemon [status]
trirouter daemon enable|disable [-n]
trirouter daemon start|stop
```

By default every Claude Code hook starts a Python process (about 0.3-0.5 s on Windows before any routing happens). With the daemon enabled, Claude Code sends its hooks as HTTP requests to a small trirouter server on 127.0.0.1 (port: config.json daemon.port, default 47621) that keeps the router loaded and its connection to JEV open; a hook then takes a few tens of milliseconds. Requests need a random token that only ~/.trirouter/state/daemon.json and Claude's settings.json hold. The SessionStart hook stays a command hook and starts the daemon when it is not running; source and config changes are reloaded by the running daemon. If the daemon is down, Claude Code goes on without the router context until the next session start. Codex and Antigravity keep their command hooks.

Subcommands: status (default), enable, disable, start, stop.

| Flag | Value | Default | Remembered | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-h`, `--help` | - | - | - | Show this help page and exit. |

**Changes:** Changes nothing by itself; see the subcommands.

Examples:

```bash
trirouter daemon    # is it enabled and running?
trirouter daemon enable    # switch Claude's hooks to it
trirouter daemon disable    # back to command hooks
```

**Exit status:** 0 on success. 2 on a usage error (unknown or misused option, missing argument). 1 when the command ran but failed.

**See also:** [daemon enable](#daemon-enable), [doctor](#doctor)

### daemon status

Show whether the hook daemon is enabled and answering.

```
trirouter daemon [status]
```

Prints the hook transport (command or http), whether the daemon answers on its port, its process id, start time and answer time, and whether Claude's settings.json carries the daemon's token.

| Flag | Value | Default | Remembered | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-h`, `--help` | - | - | - | Show this help page and exit. |

**Changes:** Changes nothing.

Examples:

```bash
trirouter daemon status    # the report
```

**Exit status:** 0 on success. 2 on a usage error (unknown or misused option, missing argument). 1 when the command ran but failed.

**See also:** [daemon enable](#daemon-enable), [daemon start](#daemon-start)

### daemon enable

Send Claude Code's hooks to the daemon over HTTP.

```
trirouter daemon enable [-n]
```

Sets hooks.transport = http in config.json, starts the daemon and rewrites trirouter's Claude Code hooks in ~/.claude/settings.json as http hooks (SessionStart stays a command hook; a .bak of the original is kept). Takes effect in new and running sessions after Claude Code re-reads its settings.

| Flag | Value | Default | Remembered | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-n`, `--dry-run` | - | off | no | Show what would change and change nothing, config.json included. |
| `-h`, `--help` | - | - | - | Show this help page and exit. |

**Changes:** Changes files; preview with --dry-run.

Examples:

```bash
trirouter daemon enable    # switch
trirouter daemon enable -n    # preview
```

**Exit status:** 0 on success. 2 on a usage error (unknown or misused option, missing argument). 1 when the command ran but failed.

**See also:** [daemon disable](#daemon-disable), [daemon status](#daemon-status)

### daemon disable

Back to command hooks; stop the daemon.

```
trirouter daemon disable [-n]
```

Sets hooks.transport = command, rewrites trirouter's Claude Code hooks as command hooks and stops the daemon.

| Flag | Value | Default | Remembered | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-n`, `--dry-run` | - | off | no | Show what would change and change nothing, config.json included. |
| `-h`, `--help` | - | - | - | Show this help page and exit. |

**Changes:** Changes files; preview with --dry-run.

Examples:

```bash
trirouter daemon disable    # switch back
```

**Exit status:** 0 on success. 2 on a usage error (unknown or misused option, missing argument). 1 when the command ran but failed.

**See also:** [daemon enable](#daemon-enable)

### daemon start

Start the hook daemon now.

```
trirouter daemon start
```

Starts the daemon in the background unless it already runs (the SessionStart hook does this by itself when the transport is http).

| Flag | Value | Default | Remembered | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-h`, `--help` | - | - | - | Show this help page and exit. |

**Changes:** Starts a background process.

Examples:

```bash
trirouter daemon start    # start it
```

**Exit status:** 0 when it answers. 1 when it did not start (see ~/.trirouter/logs/daemon.log).

**See also:** [daemon stop](#daemon-stop), [daemon status](#daemon-status)

### daemon stop

Stop the hook daemon.

```
trirouter daemon stop
```

Stops the running daemon. With the http transport still enabled the next Claude Code session start starts it again; use `daemon disable` to switch it off for good.

| Flag | Value | Default | Remembered | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-h`, `--help` | - | - | - | Show this help page and exit. |

**Changes:** Stops a background process.

Examples:

```bash
trirouter daemon stop    # stop it
```

**Exit status:** 0 when no daemon runs afterwards. 1 otherwise.

**See also:** [daemon start](#daemon-start), [daemon disable](#daemon-disable)

## learn

Train the local routing model on JEV's past decisions.

```
trirouter learn [-n]
```

Trains a small local classifier (Naive Bayes, standard library only) on the decisions JEV made for your own prompts (~/.trirouter/logs/routing.jsonl) plus the repository's labelled evaluation prompts, measures it by cross-validation against JEV's routing, and saves it to ~/.trirouter/state/distilled.json. The hooks use it only when it is enabled: when a confidence threshold exists at which it routes like JEV often enough (tier agreement and coverage targets); a confident prediction then skips the JEV call (about 0.6 s and its fee). With too little or too noisy data it is saved disabled and changes nothing. It is retrained by itself in the daily background check once enough new decisions were logged. ROUTER_DISTILLED=0 switches it off.

| Flag | Value | Default | Remembered | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-n`, `--dry-run` | - | off | no | Show what would change and change nothing, config.json included. |
| `-h`, `--help` | - | - | - | Show this help page and exit. |

**Changes:** Writes ~/.trirouter/state/distilled.json; preview with --dry-run.

Examples:

```bash
trirouter learn    # train, measure and save
trirouter learn --dry-run    # only measure
```

**Exit status:** 0 on success. 2 on a usage error (unknown or misused option, missing argument). 1 when the command ran but failed.

**See also:** [route](#route), [doctor](#doctor)

## doctor

Read-only health report.

```
trirouter doctor
```

Checks the tools (installed, version, logged in; Antigravity is asked for its model list to tell, which can take a minute), hooks, MCP entries, skill hub and agents, configuration, interpreters, the `trirouter` command, the quarantine and recent router activity. Problems are marked [!!] with the command that fixes them.

| Flag | Value | Default | Remembered | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-h`, `--help` | - | - | - | Show this help page and exit. |

**Changes:** Changes nothing.

Examples:

```bash
trirouter doctor    # print the report
```

**Exit status:** 0 always: read the [!!] lines for problems. 2 on a usage error.

**See also:** [setup](#setup), [skills](#skills)

## route

The routing decision for one prompt or sub-task.

```
trirouter route [--provider=NAME] [--json] [--] TEXT...
```

Runs the same pipeline as the hooks for one prompt, with no side effects (no queue state, no log). With no TEXT the prompt is read from stdin. Without --json it prints the [router] instruction; with --json one object: model, effort, agent, tier, task, difficulty, extra_agents, destructive, skill, verify, lang, backend, text, note. For Claude, model is always concrete: a tier that answers in-session reports sonnet. #norouter / #privat prompts are not routed. `route` must be the first argument; everything after `--` is prompt text.

Arguments: TEXT... the prompt (free-form; quote it or use --).

| Flag | Value | Default | Remembered | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--provider` | `NAME` | claude | no | Whose worker names and models to answer with. |
| `--json` | - | off | no | Print one JSON object instead of the instruction text. |
| `-h`, `--help` | - | - | - | Show this help page and exit. |

**Changes:** Changes nothing.

Examples:

```bash
trirouter route "add a pagination parameter to the quotes API"    # the instruction text
trirouter route --json --provider codex "fix the flaky login test"    # machine-readable
echo "refactor the parser" | trirouter route --json    # prompt from stdin
trirouter route -- --not-an-option    # text that starts with dashes
```

**Exit status:** 0 on success. 2 on a usage error (unknown option, empty prompt). 1 on an unexpected error.

**See also:** [doctor](#doctor)

## uninstall

Remove hooks, MCP entries, remote access and the trirouter command.

```
trirouter uninstall [-n]
```

Removes the router's hooks and MCP entries from Claude Code, Codex and Antigravity, the remote-access services, the `trirouter` launcher with its PATH entry and the tab completion in your shell profiles. Your skills stay in ~/.skills (and linked).

| Flag | Value | Default | Remembered | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `-n`, `--dry-run` | - | off | no | Show what would change and change nothing, config.json included. |
| `-h`, `--help` | - | - | - | Show this help page and exit. |

**Changes:** Changes files; preview with --dry-run.

Examples:

```bash
trirouter uninstall --dry-run    # show what would be removed
trirouter uninstall    # remove it
```

**Exit status:** 0 on success. 2 on a usage error (unknown or misused option, missing argument). 1 when the command ran but failed.

**See also:** [setup](#setup), [remote](#remote)

## help

Show the manual of a command.

```
trirouter help [COMMAND [SUBCOMMAND]]
trirouter help --markdown
```

Prints the man-page-like help of a command. `trirouter <command> --help` does the same. With --markdown it prints the complete reference (docs/cli.md).

Arguments: COMMAND a command name; SUBCOMMAND for quarantine.

| Flag | Value | Default | Remembered | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--markdown` | - | off | no | Print the whole reference as Markdown (this is how docs/cli.md is generated). |
| `-h`, `--help` | - | - | - | Show this help page and exit. |

**Changes:** Changes nothing.

Examples:

```bash
trirouter help    # the command list
trirouter help skills    # the skills page
trirouter help quarantine purge    # a subcommand
trirouter help --markdown > docs/cli.md    # regenerate the reference
```

**Exit status:** 0 on success. 2 on a usage error (unknown or misused option, missing argument). 1 when the command ran but failed.

**See also:** [doctor](#doctor)
